```{python}
#| include: false
# =============================================================================
# SETUP CELL -- runs once, shows nothing. Every card below reads from the
# objects created here, so every number on the dashboard is computed from
# the data, never typed by hand.
#
# It repeats, in one place, the steps of the project scripts:
#   03_unit_root_tests.py  -> unit_root_table
#   04_break_tests.py      -> chow_table, break_table
#   05_period_analysis.py  -> period_table
#   07_forecast.py         -> forecasts, eval_table
# =============================================================================
import ast
import contextlib
import io
import sys
import warnings
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import Markdown
from statsmodels.tools.sm_exceptions import InterpolationWarning
from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import adfuller, kpss, zivot_andrews

warnings.simplefilter("ignore", InterpolationWarning)

# Quarto runs index.qmd from inside dashboard/, so everything else in the
# project is one level up. Forward slashes work on Windows, Mac and Linux.
DATA_PATH = Path("../data/clean/lfpr_women_by_age.csv")

# The test functions (Chow, QLR, Bai-Perron, Diebold-Mariano) live in
# code/functions.py. Adding that folder to the path lets us import the SAME
# functions the paper uses instead of copying them here.
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True   # do not leave a __pycache__ folder in code/
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("../code").resolve()))
from functions import (run_chow_test, run_qlr_test, detect_multiple_breaks,
                       dm_test)

# --- Data ---------------------------------------------------------------------
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH, index_col="year")
dy_all = df.diff().dropna()          # transformed series: annual change (pp)

LABELS = {"age_16plus": "16+ (aggregate)", "age_16_24": "16-24",
          "age_25_34": "25-34", "age_35_44": "35-44", "age_45_54": "45-54",
          "age_55_64": "55-64", "age_65plus": "65+"}

# One fixed color per age group, used on every chart. The aggregate is dark
# and dashed so it reads as the benchmark, not as one more age group.
COLORS = {"age_16plus": "#14313A", "age_16_24": "#00A3A6",
          "age_25_34": "#1D5FBF", "age_35_44": "#EDA100",
          "age_45_54": "#7A4FBF", "age_55_64": "#E8590C",
          "age_65plus": "#C2417A"}
TEAL, BLUE, YELLOW, ORANGE, INK = "#00A3A6", "#1D5FBF", "#EDA100", "#E8590C", "#14313A"
GRID = "#E6ECEC"

ANDREWS_5PCT = 8.85   # Andrews (1993) 5% critical value, one restriction, 15% trimming

# --- Unit-root tests (script 03) ------------------------------------------------
ur_rows = []
for col in df.columns:
    for form, series, reg in [("levels", df[col], "ct"),
                              ("differences", df[col].diff().dropna(), "c")]:
        adf_stat, adf_p, *_ = adfuller(series, regression=reg, autolag="BIC")
        kpss_stat, kpss_p, *_ = kpss(series, regression=reg, nlags="auto")
        za_stat, za_p, crit, lags, break_idx = zivot_andrews(
            series, trim=0.15, maxlag=4, regression=reg, autolag="BIC")
        ur_rows.append({"Age group": LABELS[col], "Form": form,
                        "ADF stat": f"{adf_stat:.2f}", "ADF p": f"{adf_p:.3f}",
                        "KPSS stat": f"{kpss_stat:.2f}", "KPSS p": f"{kpss_p:.3f}",
                        "ZA stat": f"{za_stat:.2f}", "ZA p": f"{za_p:.3f}",
                        "ZA break": int(series.index[break_idx])})
unit_root_table = pd.DataFrame(ur_rows)

# --- Break tests (script 04) ----------------------------------------------------
# Candidate dates for the Chow test, chosen from the raw-series figure.
CANDIDATES = {"age_16plus": [1999], "age_16_24": [1987, 2000],
              "age_25_34": [1972], "age_35_44": [], "age_45_54": [],
              "age_55_64": [], "age_65plus": [1985]}

chow_rows, break_rows = [], []
bp_years = {}          # Bai-Perron break years per series
qlr_res = {}           # QLR break year and F per series

# The functions print their results; here we only want the numbers, so the
# printed output is captured and thrown away.
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
    for col in df.columns:
        dy = df[col].diff().dropna()
        for year in CANDIDATES[col]:
            res = run_chow_test(dy.values, dy.index.get_loc(year))
            chow_rows.append({"Age group": LABELS[col], "Candidate year": year,
                              "F-statistic": f"{res['f_stat']:.2f}",
                              "p-value": f"{res['p_value']:.3f}",
                              "Result": "Break" if res["reject_h0"] else "No break"})
        qlr = run_qlr_test(dy.values, trim=0.15)
        bp = detect_multiple_breaks(dy.values, min_size=12)
        qlr_res[col] = {"year": int(dy.index[qlr["break_index"]]),
                        "f_stat": float(qlr["f_stat"])}
        bp_years[col] = [int(dy.index[b]) for b in bp]
        break_rows.append({
            "Age group": LABELS[col],
            "QLR break year": qlr_res[col]["year"],
            "QLR F": f"{qlr_res[col]['f_stat']:.2f}",
            "Significant (5%)": "Yes" if qlr_res[col]["f_stat"] > ANDREWS_5PCT else "No",
            "Bai-Perron breaks": ", ".join(map(str, bp_years[col])) or "None"})

chow_table = pd.DataFrame(chow_rows)
break_table = pd.DataFrame(break_rows)

n_series_with_break = sum(len(v) > 0 for v in bp_years.values())
n_breaks_total = sum(len(v) for v in bp_years.values())

# --- Periods between breaks (script 05) -------------------------------------------
period_rows = []
periods = {}           # per series: list of (start, end, slope, intercept)
for col in df.columns:
    starts = [int(df.index.min())] + bp_years[col]
    ends = [b - 1 for b in bp_years[col]] + [int(df.index.max())]
    periods[col] = []
    for start, end in zip(starts, ends):
        seg = df.loc[start:end, col]
        adf_p = adfuller(seg, regression="ct", maxlag=2, autolag="AIC")[1]
        kpss_p = kpss(seg, regression="ct", nlags="auto")[1]
        trend_stat = adf_p < 0.05 and kpss_p >= 0.05
        slope, intercept = np.polyfit(seg.index.values, seg.values, 1)
        periods[col].append((start, end, slope, intercept))
        period_rows.append({"Age group": LABELS[col], "Start": start, "End": end,
                            "Years": len(seg),
                            "Classification": "Trend-stationary" if trend_stat
                                              else "Diff-stationary",
                            "Slope (pp/yr)": f"{slope:+.2f}",
                            "Mean Δ (pp/yr)": f"{seg.diff().mean():+.2f}"})
period_table = pd.DataFrame(period_rows)

# --- Forecast comparison, aggregate 16+ (script 07) ---------------------------------
SERIES = "age_16plus"
LAST_TRAIN_YEAR = 2014
TEST_YEARS = list(range(2015, 2026))
COVID_YEARS = (2020, 2021)

y = df[SERIES]
dy_train = y.diff().dropna().loc[:LAST_TRAIN_YEAR]

with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
    qlr_train = run_qlr_test(dy_train.values)
fc_break_year = int(dy_train.index[qlr_train["break_index"]])

mu_full = dy_train.mean()                       # (a) ignores the break
mu_post = dy_train.loc[fc_break_year:].mean()   # (b) uses the break

actual = y.loc[TEST_YEARS].values
y_prev = y.loc[[t - 1 for t in TEST_YEARS]].values
fc_full = y_prev + mu_full
fc_post = y_prev + mu_post
e_full = actual - fc_full
e_post = actual - fc_post

no_covid = np.array([t not in COVID_YEARS for t in TEST_YEARS])
samples = {"All years (2015-2025)": np.ones(len(TEST_YEARS), dtype=bool),
           "Excluding 2020-2021": no_covid}
eval_rows = []
dm_all = None
for label, mask in samples.items():
    ea, eb = e_full[mask], e_post[mask]
    hln = dm_test(ea, eb, h=1, small_sample=True)
    if dm_all is None:
        dm_all = hln
    eval_rows.append({"Evaluation sample": label, "N": int(mask.sum()),
                      "RMSE full-sample drift": f"{np.sqrt(np.mean(ea**2)):.3f}",
                      "RMSE post-break drift": f"{np.sqrt(np.mean(eb**2)):.3f}",
                      "Mean loss diff.": f"{hln['d_bar']:+.3f}",
                      "DM (HLN)": f"{hln['dm_stat']:.2f}",
                      "p-value": f"{hln['p_value']:.3f}"})
eval_table = pd.DataFrame(eval_rows)
rmse_full = np.sqrt(np.mean(e_full**2))
rmse_post = np.sqrt(np.mean(e_post**2))


# --- Helpers used by the cards --------------------------------------------------------
def show_table(table, note=""):
    """Render a DataFrame as a clean table inside a card, with an optional
    note underneath (kept in the same card as the table)."""
    # disable_numparse keeps numbers exactly as formatted (0.000, not 0)
    text = table.to_markdown(index=False, disable_numparse=True)
    if note:
        text += f"\n\n*Notes:* {note}"
    return Markdown(text)


def base_layout(fig, ytitle, xrange=None):
    """Shared look for every figure: light grid, legend on top, hover by year."""
    fig.update_layout(
        template="plotly_white", hovermode="x unified",
        margin=dict(l=55, r=20, t=30, b=40),
        font=dict(family="Inter, Arial, sans-serif", size=12, color=INK),
        legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, x=0),
        xaxis=dict(title="Year", range=xrange, gridcolor=GRID, showline=True,
                   linecolor="#9AA7A7"),
        yaxis=dict(title=ytitle, gridcolor=GRID, zerolinecolor="#9AA7A7"))
    return fig


def lines_by_age(data, ytitle, fmt):
    """One line per age group, same color everywhere."""
    fig = go.Figure()
    for col in data.columns:
        is_agg = col == "age_16plus"
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=data.index, y=data[col], name=LABELS[col], mode="lines",
            line=dict(color=COLORS[col], width=3 if is_agg else 2,
                      dash="dash" if is_agg else "solid"),
            hovertemplate=f"%{{y:{fmt}}}"))
    return base_layout(fig, ytitle,
                       xrange=[int(data.index.min()), int(data.index.max())])
```

#| title: "About this project"
Markdown("""
**Question.** Did the labor force participation rate of U.S. women experience
structural breaks, did they happen at different times for women of different
ages, and does detecting them improve forecasts?

**Method.** Each series is I(1), so it is modeled as a random walk with drift.
A break is a change in the drift, tested on first differences with the Chow,
QLR and Bai-Perron procedures.

**Data.** U.S. Department of Labor, Women's Bureau (BLS Current Population
Survey), annual averages.
""")

### Column {width=56%}

```{python}
#| title: "Participation rate, Bai-Perron break years and period trends — choose an age group"
# Note: in a dashboard, Quarto displays the value of EVERY top-level line,
# not only the last one. Calls that return the figure are therefore assigned
# to `_`, and the figure is shown once, by the final line `fig`.
# One figure holding all seven age groups; the dropdown shows one at a time.
# Each age group contributes three traces: the series, the fitted trend
# within each period, and the vertical break lines.
fig = go.Figure()
cols = list(df.columns)
for i, col in enumerate(cols):
    s = df[col]
    lo, hi = s.min(), s.max()
    pad = 0.08 * (hi - lo)
    visible = i == 0

    _ = fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=s.index, y=s.values, mode="lines", name="Participation rate",
        line=dict(color=TEAL, width=2), visible=visible,
        hovertemplate="%{y:.1f}%"))

    # Trend within each period (None separates the periods)
    tx, ty, labx, laby, labt = [], [], [], [], []
    for start, end, slope, intercept in periods[col]:
        yrs = np.arange(start, end + 1)
        tx += list(yrs) + [None]
        ty += list(slope * yrs + intercept) + [None]
        labx.append((start + end) / 2)
        laby.append(hi + pad)
        labt.append(f"{slope:+.2f} pp/yr")
    _ = fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=tx, y=ty, mode="lines", name="Trend within period",
        line=dict(color=ORANGE, width=2.5), visible=visible,
        hovertemplate="trend %{y:.1f}%"))

    bx, by = [], []
    for b in bp_years[col]:
        bx += [b, b, None]
        by += [lo - pad, hi + 2 * pad, None]
    _ = fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=bx or [None], y=by or [None], mode="lines",
        name="Break year" if bp_years[col] else "Break year (none found)",
        line=dict(color=INK, width=1.5, dash="dash"), visible=visible,
        hoverinfo="skip"))

    # Slope of each period, written above the series
    _ = fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=labx, y=laby, mode="text", text=labt, showlegend=False,
        textfont=dict(color=INK, size=12), visible=visible, hoverinfo="skip"))

TRACES_PER_SERIES = 4
buttons = []
for i, col in enumerate(cols):
    mask = [j // TRACES_PER_SERIES == i for j in range(len(fig.data))]
    found = ", ".join(map(str, bp_years[col])) or "none"
    buttons.append(dict(label=LABELS[col], method="update",
                        args=[{"visible": mask},
                              {"title.text": f"Women {LABELS[col]} · breaks: {found}"}]))

_ = base_layout(fig, "Participation rate (%)",
                xrange=[int(df.index.min()), int(df.index.max())])
first_found = ", ".join(map(str, bp_years[cols[0]])) or "none"
_ = fig.update_layout(
    title=dict(text=f"Women {LABELS[cols[0]]} · breaks: {first_found}",
               x=0.99, xanchor="right", y=0.98, font=dict(size=13)),
    margin=dict(t=70),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="top", y=-0.16, x=0),
    updatemenus=[dict(type="dropdown", buttons=buttons, direction="down",
                      x=0, xanchor="left", y=1.18, yanchor="top",
                      bgcolor="white", bordercolor=TEAL)])
fig
```

    "Slope: linear trend fitted within the period. Mean Δ: average annual change."))

    x=context.index, y=context.values, mode="lines", name="Actual",
    line=dict(color=INK, width=2.5), hovertemplate="%{y:.1f}%"))

    x=TEST_YEARS, y=fc_full, mode="lines+markers",
    name=f"Full-sample drift ({mu_full:+.2f} pp/yr)",
    line=dict(color=BLUE, width=2, dash="dash"),
    marker=dict(size=8, symbol="circle"), hovertemplate="%{y:.2f}%"))
_ = fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=TEST_YEARS, y=fc_post, mode="lines+markers",
    name=f"Post-{fc_break_year} drift ({mu_post:+.2f} pp/yr)",

_ = fig.add_vline(x=LAST_TRAIN_YEAR + 0.5, line=dict(color="#9AA7A7", dash="dot"))
_ = fig.add_annotation(x=LAST_TRAIN_YEAR + 0.6, y=0.03, yref="paper", xanchor="left",

base_layout(fig, "Participation rate (%)", xrange=[2005, 2025.3])

Both forecasts are a random walk with drift estimated through 2014 and

```{=html}
<!-- Plotly measures the width of its legend and dropdown labels when a
     figure is first drawn. While the dashboard is still loading (or the
     figure sits on a hidden page or tab) those widths come back as zero and
     the labels overlap. Nudging the font size once the figure is visible
     makes Plotly measure the labels again. -->
<script>
(function () {
  function refreshVisible() {
    if (!window.Plotly) return;
    document.querySelectorAll(".plotly-graph-div").forEach(function (div) {
      if (div.offsetWidth > 0 && !div.dataset.refreshed) {
        div.dataset.refreshed = "1";
        window.Plotly.relayout(div, {"font.size": 12.5});
      }
    });
  }
  window.addEventListener("load", function () { setTimeout(refreshVisible, 400); });
  document.addEventListener("shown.bs.tab", function () { setTimeout(refreshVisible, 150); });
})();
</script>
```
